title: This Whale Held Its Breath Longer Than a Movie
subject: Cuvier's beaked whale

scenes.text: One whale holds its breath longer than most movies last. How?
A Cuvier's beaked whale was tracked diving to 9,816 feet, almost two miles.
Another stayed under for 138 minutes. That's over two hours without a breath.
Its lungs collapse around two hundred meters down. So it doesn't store oxygen in them.
It stores it in blood and muscle instead, packed so full of oxygen carriers they look almost black.
So the longest breath-hold of any mammal comes from a whale that barely uses its lungs.

description:
One whale holds its breath longer than most movies last.
A Cuvier's beaked whale was tracked diving to 9,816 feet and staying under for 138 minutes in a 2014 study.
Could you hold your breath for even two minutes?
